# Named Contact Gone Quiet

`customer_support.sit.named_contact_gone_quiet` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

Owned by `customer_support.support_management.account_relationship_management`


> A named contact at a supported account has stopped writing in, and the gap is long relative to how often they used to. Nothing is broken, no clock is running, and no ticket is open — which is exactly the problem, because every instrument a support team owns is pointed at open work and this account has none. The expert reading is that silence from an account that used to file tickets is a hypothesis to be tested rather than a result to be enjoyed: either the product got better, or they found another way to get answers, or they stopped believing it was worth asking us. The test is cheap and it is not a survey — it is a specific message that references something real from their history and asks a question only they can answer. A generic check-in gets ignored, and being ignored converts a soft signal into no signal.

> champion_change, introduction and followup_sent are real substrate observation kinds. ticket_created, self_service_attempted, cancellation_threat and entitlement_expired are support-native and sit in planned_substrate.obs_kinds. The lists are unvalidated so the mixture is legal; noting it so the file is not later read as more executable than it is.
THE BASELINE IS WRONG AND IT IS THE BEST AVAILABLE. reply_cadence is learned from reply latency inside threads, not from how often an account opens new contacts. What this situation actually wants is contact_rate_per_account, which exists in planned_substrate.baselines and is emitted by nothing. Until it ships, the narrowing above is a proxy: it will be roughly right for accounts whose support relationship runs through email threads and roughly wrong for accounts that live in a portal or a chat widget, where the pipeline sees nothing at all and this situation therefore never fires — which is a quiet failure worth remembering, because those are usually the higher-volume accounts.
champion_change appears under decay and deserves its own read: silence plus a departed contact is not one signal, it is the specific failure where a relationship had exactly one thread and nobody inherited it. That case is more urgent than plain quiet and today the two are indistinguishable at this level; separating them wants a churn_risk_from_support type, which is in planned_substrate.
